senses.gloss: f. (טלל, v. preced., = אִטְלֵיס q. v.) resting place, road-station. Y’lamd. to Deut. IV, 30 (quot. in Ar.) עשה אסטולי וכתוב וכ׳ he put up a station for travellers, over which was written, “When this people shall go up &c.” (I Kings XII, 27).—Pl. אִסְטַלִּיוֹת (fr. אִסְטַלִּית).
units: <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 23">Num. R. s. 23</cite> <he>העמד להם א׳</he> put up for them (the unintentional murderers fleeing to the place of refuge) resting stations <he>ובכל א … יות וכ׳</he> (read <cite ref="A02381"><he>אסטלית</he></cite> or <cite ref="A02375"><he>אסטל</he></cite>) and let there be an inscription over each of them &c. Tanḥ. Masé 11; ed. Bub. 8; <cite ref="A01217"><he>אִיטְלִיסִיּוֹת</he></cite>, <cite ref="A01092"><he>אִיטְלֵיס</he></cite>.—Y’lamd. to Deut. III, 9 <he>עמון ומואב עשו אִיסְטְלִים</he> Am. a. Moab erected resting stations for the passing Israelites (quot. in Ar. s. v. <cite ref="A03124"><he>ארך</he></cite> 5).
